They make from this cordage with which they sew up ships instead of iron nails.' Describing the betel (paan), he noted: 'The betel is a tree which is cultivated in the same manner as the grape-vine... The betel has no fruit and is grown only for the sake of its leaves... The manner of its use is that before eating it one takes the areca nut, which is like a nutmeg, breaks it into small pellets and puts these in his mouth and chews them. Then he takes the leaves of betel, puts a little chalk (lime) on them, and chews them together.'"

According to Ibn Battuta's eyewitness description, what ingredients were chewed together in the consumption of paan?
